title: Best Trading Journal for Tradovate Users (and How to Import Your Trades)
excerpt: Trade on Tradovate? Here is what a journal must do for prop firm traders, how to export your Tradovate trades to CSV, and how to get them into Zentrade without retyping everything.
seoTitle: Best Trading Journal for Tradovate Users (2026): Import Trades via CSV
seoDescription: Looking for a Tradovate trading journal? Learn what to look for, how to export Tradovate trades as CSV, and how to track prop firm rules like drawdown and consistency.
author: Zentrade Team

content.text: The best trading journal for Tradovate users is one that ingests your Tradovate trade history, tracks your prop firm rules (drawdown, consistency, daily loss) and records why you took each trade. Tradovate itself shows fills and P&L, but it does not tell you whether your behavior is repeating a losing pattern. A journal does.

Tradovate is the execution platform behind many futures prop firm accounts, including Apex Trader Funding evaluations. That makes it the place where most evaluation trades happen, and a poor place to review them. This guide explains what to demand from a journal, how to export your Tradovate data, and where Zentrade fits today. We will be direct about one limit: Zentrade does not yet connect to Tradovate automatically.
What a Tradovate Journal Must Do for Prop Firm Traders
A spreadsheet can store trades. An evaluation-grade journal has to answer harder questions: how close am I to my drawdown floor, is one day carrying my profit, and what am I doing after a loss?

items: Rule tracking: trailing drawdown, daily loss and consistency metrics visible next to your P&L, not buried in a notes tab.
Trade-level context: setup, session, emotional state, and whether you followed your plan.
Pattern detection: performance by hour, instrument (NQ, ES, MNQ, GC) and setup, so you stop trading your worst window.
Multiple accounts: if you run several evaluations or a funded account plus a live account, each needs its own equity curve.
Low friction: if logging takes 20 minutes, you will skip it after a bad day, which is exactly when you need it.

How to Export Your Trades from Tradovate

Tradovate lets you export trade data to CSV from its reporting tools. Menu names can change between app versions, so treat these steps as a guide and check Tradovate's own help center if a label differs.

items: Log in to Tradovate and open the account you want to review. If you trade through a prop firm, make sure you are on the evaluation or funded account, not a demo.
Open the reports or account history section and choose a performance or fills report for your date range.
Export the result as a CSV file. Keep the original file untouched as a backup.
Open the CSV and confirm it contains date and time, symbol, side, quantity, entry price, exit price and P&L. If a column is missing, export a different report type.
Import the file into your journal and review the column mapping before confirming.
Time zones: exports may be in a different time zone than you trade. Check one trade against your platform before trusting hour-of-day analysis.
Partial fills: one order can appear as several rows. Make sure the journal groups fills into a single trade.
Commissions and fees: confirm whether P&L is gross or net, because your prop firm measures net.

A 10-Minute Post-Session Routine for Tradovate Traders

items: Export or enter the day's trades.
Tag each trade: planned setup or impulse.
Write one sentence on how you felt before the biggest loss.
Check distance to your drawdown floor and your best-day share of total profit.
Decide one rule for tomorrow, such as no trades after two consecutive losses.

content.text: A journal does not make a strategy profitable and cannot guarantee you pass an evaluation. It makes your process visible so you can fix what is actually breaking it.

faqItems.q: Does Zentrade connect directly to Tradovate?
faqItems.a: Not yet. A direct Tradovate integration is in development and listed as coming soon, with no release date. Today you can export your Tradovate trades to CSV and import them on the Professional or ZenMode plan, or log trades manually on any plan.

faqItems.q: Which Zentrade plan includes CSV import?
faqItems.a: CSV import is included in Professional ($29/mo) and ZenMode ($59/mo). Starter ($9/mo) and Free use manual entry and CSV export.

faqItems.q: Can I journal multiple Apex or Tradovate accounts?
faqItems.a: Yes. Starter supports 2 accounts and Professional and ZenMode support unlimited accounts, each with its own metrics.

faqItems.q: Is the journal useful if I only trade evaluations?
faqItems.a: Yes. Evaluations are where consistency and drawdown mistakes cost you the most, so tracking them per account is where a journal pays for itself.

faqItems.q: What should my Tradovate CSV include?
faqItems.a: At minimum: date and time, symbol, side, quantity, entry and exit price, and P&L. Check whether P&L includes commissions, since prop firms measure net results.
